title: Microeconomics for Finance
text:
This course provides students with relevant microeconomic methods to tackle finance issues. The course covers 24 hours of material and is designed for first-year Master in Finance students at Paris Dauphine University - PSL.


The course consists of four main topics:

Equilibrium in an Exchange Economy - Understanding how markets allocate resources through voluntary exchange
Decision Making under Uncertainty - Expected utility theory and risk preferences
Equilibrium in Markets for Securities - Asset pricing and portfolio theory
Investment Decisions under Market Imperfections - Asymmetric information and agency problems






Topic 1: Exchange Economy
Understanding the fundamentals of market equilibrium with a focus on exchange between agents.


Topic 2: Decision under Uncertainty
Expected utility theory, risk aversion, and portfolio choice.


Topic 3: Securities Markets
Asset pricing models, CAPM, and market equilibrium concepts.


Topic 4: Market Imperfections
Asymmetric information, principal-agent problems, and real-world market frictions.






Instructor: Juan F. Imbet
Institution: Paris Dauphine University - PSL
Level: Master in Finance, 1st Year
Duration: 24 hours
Evaluation: Mid-term and final exams




By the end of this course, students will be able to:

Understand the fundamental concepts of microeconomic theory as applied to finance
Analyze market equilibrium under different conditions
Apply expected utility theory to decision-making under uncertainty
Comprehend asset pricing models and their implications
Recognize the impact of market imperfections on investment decisions





Basic knowledge of microeconomics
Familiarity with mathematical concepts (calculus, probability)
Understanding of financial instruments


This course builds upon the foundational work of previous instructors while incorporating modern developments in financial economics.

title: About
text:
Juan F. Imbet
Assistant Professor
Department of Finance
Paris Dauphine University - PSL



This 24-hour course in Microeconomics for Finance aims to equip students with essential microeconomic tools for analyzing financial markets and decision-making. The course bridges theoretical microeconomics with practical applications in finance.



Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:

Apply microeconomic principles to financial decision-making
Understand market equilibrium concepts in financial contexts
Analyze decision-making under uncertainty using expected utility theory
Comprehend asset pricing models and their implications
Recognize the impact of market imperfections on investment decisions




The course is divided into four main modules, each building upon the previous one:

Foundation: Exchange economy and basic equilibrium concepts
Risk and Uncertainty: Decision theory and risk preferences
Asset Markets: Pricing and portfolio theory
Real-World Applications: Market imperfections and agency problems




All course materials are provided in interactive HTML format using Quarto and Reveal.js, allowing for an engaging learning experience with embedded mathematical expressions and visualizations.



For questions about the course content or materials, please contact the instructor.



This course builds upon the foundational work of previous instructors and incorporates modern developments in financial economics and teaching methodologies.
